findings.issue: New team-page UI was never visually inspected (no browser commands, no screenshots) — verification relied entirely on the Playwright suite
findings.suggestion: Boot the built server and take a quick screenshot of /team (empty and populated) to catch visual regressions the tests don't assert

findings.issue: Wrote an import from `@ngrx/store` — a dependency that doesn't exist in this project — and had to fix it one turn later (trace turns 22-23)
findings.suggestion: Check the existing imports/dependencies before generating new files; the codebase uses signals, not NgRx

findings.issue: Initial normalizeTeam contained nonsense logic (`unique.has(unique.size > 0 ? trimmed : '')`), patched one turn later (trace turns 16-17)
findings.suggestion: Self-review generated code before writing it to disk

findings.issue: Passed the cookie string to normalizeTeam as a single-element array instead of splitting on ','; caused 4 team-test failures and a turn of wrong hypotheses (trace turns 33-35)
findings.suggestion: When new code fails immediately, trace its data flow (cookie join vs split) before blaming SSR/hydration races

findings.issue: Ran `npm test -- --run` in app/ which failed with 'Unknown argument: run' without first checking the test script
findings.suggestion: Read the script definition in package.json before guessing CLI flags; `CI=1 npm test` (the next attempt) was correct

findings.issue: Grepped node_modules/@angular/core before dependencies were installed (command exited code 2)
findings.suggestion: Run npm install first when node_modules is absent; it did recover correctly next turn

summary: A disciplined, well-planned session: the agent understood the SSR/hydration/localStorage constraint before coding, designed a cookie-backed team store, and implemented it in one linear pass. Debugging of the single test regression was systematic if briefly flailing. Weak spots are small: three careless first-writes needing immediate fixes, two failed bash calls, and no manual visual check of the new UI.
